q1.question: EXIT state at canonical V4 no_legal_move dead ends
q1.extra_category_explanation: seen_not_currently_visible is necessary: EXIT had entered the hand earlier, but a later no-play refresh had cycled it out of the current hand before terminal no_legal_move.
q1.interpretation: No canonical V4 no_legal_move loss ended before EXIT had ever been seen. Only one ended with EXIT currently visible but unplayable; 23 had seen EXIT earlier but no longer had it visible, and 15 had already placed EXIT. Thus terminal dead ends are not explained by one simple 'EXIT never appeared' mechanism.

q2.question: Are canonical V4 no_legal_move failures near-wins?
q2.interpretation: Yes, many V4 dead ends are structurally very close to victory: all 39 are equipment-ready, 35 are water-clear, 32 are at <=5 open tunnels, and 28 satisfy all three. But the failure is not solely loss of EXIT access: 15/39 already placed EXIT before dead-ending, while 24/39 still lacked a placed EXIT.

q3.question: Mechanism on all canonical V4-only wins
q3.interpretation: The repeated advantage mechanism is genuinely bounded merge setup followed by consolidation: all 11/11 canonical V4-only wins have positive bounded setup, later consolidation, EXIT placement, and eventual full closure in that order. Their topology stays controlled (mean maximum open tunnels 8.09; every listed seed peaks at <=10), whereas WaterSpaceV3 on the same seeds reaches a much larger mean maximum frontier (17.18) and fails to close.

q4.question: Why V4 loses on every canonical WaterSpaceV3-only winning seed
interpretation: Seed 2067: V4 places EXIT but exhausts the deck with water clear and 12 open tunnels; WaterSpaceV3 wins. This is post-EXIT topology over-expansion, not EXIT access.
Seed 2241: V4 places EXIT but exhausts the deck with 19 open tunnels and 1 visible water; WaterSpaceV3 wins. Both unresolved water and a very large frontier remain.
Seed 2272: V4 places EXIT but exhausts the deck with 20 open tunnels and 2 visible water; WaterSpaceV3 wins. Again the loss is post-EXIT branching plus unresolved water.
Across all three, EXIT timing is effectively the same between policies; V4's distinguishing pattern is much larger merge/setup activity and maximum open frontier.

q5.choice: B — mechanisms remain entangled; V5 is premature
q5.recommended_single_additional_diagnostic: On the same canonical seeds and trajectories only, split every V4 positive bounded-merge-setup event and every compaction/branching event into three EXIT phases: before EXIT is first seen, while EXIT is visible but unplaced, and after EXIT is placed. Compare those phase counts for the 11 canonical V4-only wins, the 39 V4 no_legal_move losses, and the 3 WaterSpaceV3-only wins. This tests whether a single phase gate on bounded-merge setup could preserve the winning setup→consolidation mechanism while avoiding both EXIT-access dead ends and post-EXIT over-branching. Do not change policy behavior in that diagnostic.

metric_semantics.consolidation_move: placement move with negative actual delta_open
metric_semantics.exit_visible_turn_count_before_placement: count of distinct completed-action state turns in which EXIT was visible before placement
metric_semantics.first_return_open_threshold: first state at/below threshold after previously exceeding it; avoids the trivial START state
metric_semantics.first_water_clear_after_water_seen_state: first zero-visible-water state after water had previously become visible; avoids the trivial initial water-clear state
metric_semantics.multi_attachment_move: placement whose occupied coordinates consume at least two pre-existing open-tunnel targets
metric_semantics.state_turn: number of completed actions; initial state is turn 0
